answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a bond before accepting paid jobs; a contract slashes it if the agent signs conflicting receipts for the same job. If an operator called comet creates 1,000 identities, it must fund 1,000 bonds. The capital delta grows with each alias, even at the market’s nadir, while provable cheating burns the affected bonds. Aliases remain possible, but they are neither free nor riskless.
